rationale: Fire damage to the claimant's own kitchen cabinets and smoke damage to ceilings and walls caused by the claimant's own stove malfunction is direct property damage to the claimant's own home, and is covered under the homeowners policy.
claim_summary: Policyholder: Alex Doe (POL-1001, Active Homeowners Policy, $500 deductible, $250K limit). Incident: Kitchen fire yesterday evening caused by grease flare-up on stove while sauteing; claimant extinguished with fire extinguisher. Damage: Charred kitchen cabinets above stove and smoke damage to ceiling and walls; no other rooms affected, no injuries. Classification: Property damage (confidence 1.0). Severity: Medium—moderate localized property loss requiring restoration but contained to one room with no injuries.

case_facts.description: stove fire caused by grease flare-up while sauteing onions; extinguished with fire extinguisher
case_facts.property_damage: charred kitchen cabinets above stove; smoke damage on ceiling and walls

rationale: Damage caused solely by claimant's own plumbing failure with no third-party negligence involved; hardwood floor, drywall, and contents damage are direct results of the burst supply line.
claim_summary: Policyholder Sam Patel (POL-1004, homeowners premium, $750K limit, $500 deductible) filed a property damage claim for basement flooding caused by a burst supply line under the upstairs bathroom sink that ran for approximately two days. Damage includes approximately two inches of standing water throughout the basement, buckled hardwood flooring, drywall saturated up to one foot, and ruined stored boxes. Claim classified as property_damage with 0.95 confidence and assessed as high severity due to extensive structural damage and contents loss across the entire basement.

case_facts.incident_description: Basement flooded with approximately two inches of water
case_facts.property_damage_items: Hardwood floor buckled, drywall soaked up to one foot, stored boxes ruined
case_facts.discovery_context: Claimant returned home from work trip to find flooding
case_facts.incident_cause: Burst supply line under upstairs bathroom sink, ran for approximately two days

rationale: Wind damage to the claimant's own roof shingles is direct property damage to their home, with no involvement of another party's negligence or third-party responsibility.
claim_summary: Policyholder Jordan Lee (POL-1006, homeowners premium, $1M limit, $2,500 deductible, active) reports wind damage to back porch roof overhang with four shingles blown off following high winds last weekend. No interior water damage. Estimated repair cost $400. Classified as property_damage with low severity due to minor damage amount and no injuries or secondary damage.

case_facts.damage_description: four shingles blown off, no interior water damage
